instruction: Export the essay document 'Recruitment_and_retention_of_health_professionals_across_Europe.docx' from /home/user as a PDF file.

metadata.explanation: Task requires exporting the essay document as a PDF file. Evaluator verifies: (1) PDF file exists at expected path, (2) file is valid PDF with proper magic bytes, (3) PDF has substantial content (non-zero pages and reasonable file size), (4) PDF content matches source .docx file by comparing extracted text. This ensures the PDF was properly exported from the .docx file rather than being a pre-existing or manually created file.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies all aspects of the instruction: PDF file existence, validity, content quality, and source document matching
Getter logic is comprehensive - extracts PDF file existence, validates magic bytes (%PDF), extracts page count and file size, reads and compares content from source .docx file
Metric comparison logic is sound - performs 4 progressive checks (exists, is_valid_pdf, has_content, content_matches) with appropriate partial credit scoring
Data flow is correct: getter extracts the right state (PDF file properties and content comparison with .docx), metric compares the right aspects using the extracted data
Expected value is semantically correct: {"exists": true} appropriately verifies that the PDF export was successful
Metric correctly handles expected parameter as rules dict directly (expected.get('exists', True)) - no parameter handling errors
Content verification logic is robust: compares word overlap between PDF and .docx with 50% threshold, handles edge cases where source may not exist
Edge cases are handled: checks for missing files, invalid PDFs, empty content, and provides graceful degradation with partial credit
